findings.issue_category: database credential exposed in user data
findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a PHP configuration file. User data is retained by EC2 and is accessible from the instance; moreover, the resulting file is created without restrictive permissions, exposing the database credential to local users/processes that can read it.

`publicly_accessible = true` assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, the database is unnecessarily exposed to an Internet-routable network boundary and becomes reachable if security-group rules are broadened or other network paths are introduced.
`storage_encrypted = false` leaves the RDS database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and replicas unencrypted at rest, exposing database contents if underlying storage artifacts are accessed.

No DB parameter enforces MySQL secure transport (for example, `require_secure_transport = ON`). The application connects with `mysqli_connect` without SSL options, so database credentials and application data can be transmitted unencrypted between the application and RDS.

The MySQL port is open to every address in the VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or specific required clients. Any workload in the VPC, including a compromised or newly deployed one, can attempt to connect to the database.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports to every IPv4 address. This removes egress network controls and enables unnecessary outbound communication or data exfiltration from a compromised database environment.

The policy grants the EC2 application role every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. A compromise of the application instance or its instance credentials would grant broad account-level control and access to data across those services.
